% === Limitations (ACL required, unnumbered) ===
\clearpage
\section*{Limitations}

Our study has three main limitations.
(1)~\emph{Scope}: we evaluate models up to 8B parameters across 6 architecture families, English text only (C4, Wikipedia, arXiv), and prompt-chain generation; retrain-chain dynamics may yield different boundaries.
(2)~\emph{Feature set}: the 15 statistical features provide a lower bound on $\Ktheory$; richer representations (e.g., neural probes) can extend $\Kempirical$ by one additional depth for some architectures.
(3)~\emph{Threshold sensitivity}: $\Kempirical$ varies with the decision threshold $\theta$, ranging from 2--3 at $\theta{=}0.55$ to 1 at $\theta{=}0.70$; two of ten configurations are marginal at our reference $\theta{=}0.60$.

% === Ethics Statement (ACL required, unnumbered) ===
\section*{Ethics Statement}

Generational depth estimation is intended for data curation and corpus auditing, positive-sum applications that improve training data quality.
Our experiments use the publicly available C4 corpus and do not involve personally identifiable information.
A potential dual-use concern is that depth estimation techniques could inform adversarial strategies to evade detection (e.g., by calibrating rewriting to mimic earlier-generation statistics); we note that this risk is shared by all detection research and that the binary detection boundary ($\auc \geq 0.96$ at 0v1) remains robust.
Code and data will be released upon acceptance.

\bibliography{references}

\input{appendix}
